title: Storefront and Website Resolution
readerIntent: Configure several websites and stores for one tenant and enterprise.
priorKnowledge: Understand Store, Site, CMS catalog, country, and channel concepts.
owner: Storefront owns hostname resolution and opaque trusted context; referenced modules retain their data
summary: A hostname resolves to a configured Storefront Site, Store, enterprise, tenant, country, channel, locale, currency, and catalog context that downstream modules verify for their own audience.

sections.heading: Two-website example
items: apparel.nodics.com and electronics.nodics.com belong to the same tenant and enterprise.
Each hostname maps to its own Storefront Site and Store.
Each Site selects its intended CMS content catalog, product catalog, country, channel, locale, and currency.
The websites can have completely different templates and content while reusing platform modules.
One Site may intentionally serve several Stores without duplicating CMS ownership.

sections.heading: Security and operations
items: Clients receive an opaque context handle rather than choosing trusted tenant or sourcing rules.
Inventory, Pricing, Product, CMS, and other modules validate the handle for their own audience.
Hostname aliases, activation, cache TTL, invalidation, fallback, and ambiguity policy are configurable.
Unknown, duplicate, inactive, cross-tenant, spoofed, expired, and wrong-audience contexts fail safely.
